properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22: "decision points for when a design gets to a certain point (say TRL is too low or MRL is too low or testing reveals something the designer didn't initially consider) that you can go back to the decision point or 'fork' and say, we need to go in a different direction… The feedback tool should fire on ANY feedback to the design. Positive feedback should strengthen design choices. Negative feedback should cause 'doubt' over a design decision in the graph and cause the system to determine root-cause (if appropriate) or at least see if other choices would potentially do better."

⭐ MOST OF THIS IS ALREADY DESIGNED, WHICH IS THE FIRST THING TO SAY. A thorough search on 2026-09-22 found the whole return path modelled: `cap:revise-trigger` (PLANNED) traces new evidence back through GOVERNED_BY to the Decisions that shaped the affected nodes and surfaces them as "this road may be worth re-opening"; `cap:fork-alternatives` (PLANNED) holds and re-forks the unchosen alternatives; `req:roads-not-taken` requires they be preserved and forkable; `dec:fork-point-address` makes a fork point a coordinate (decision → epoch → export hash); `dec:reopen-supersedes` says re-opening mints a new Decision that obsoletes the old rather than un-accepting it; `dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable` says the human judges in hindsight and no score is stored. The ladder goes down. It is drawn and not built.

🛑 TWO THINGS HIS ASK ADDS THAT THE DESIGN DOES **NOT** HOLD.

**(1) LOW READINESS IS NOT AN INPUT TO THE DOUBT.** `cap:revise-trigger` names exactly four triggers: a fresh structural defect, a failing verification, an accepted drift, a field-trial finding. TRL/MRL is not among them. And readiness IS built — `cap:readiness-gating` computes which epoch an increment can deliver on from a TRL/MRL assessment against a threshold the user states. So the design can already say "this is not ready enough to ship" and has no path from there to "then the decision that got us here may be worth re-opening". The two halves exist and do not speak.
    OPTIONS: (a) add readiness to revise-trigger's trigger set — smallest, and it composes two built/designed things; (b) treat a GATED_ON threshold miss as a first-class event that propagates like a drift; (c) leave it, on the ground that a low TRL is a schedule fact rather than evidence the design is wrong. ⚠️ (c) is not obviously false: a thing can be correctly designed and simply immature.

**(2) NOTHING LETS GOOD NEWS STRENGTHEN A DECISION.** The vocabulary is asymmetric. Corroboration exists only between FINDINGS — `cap:supporting-is-not-conflict` (REALIZED) reads an `alignment: supporting` on a CONTRADICTS edge so a reinforcing pair is not reported as a defect — and `dec:idea-how-should-one-finding-say-it-corroborates-another` is still open about how ugly that is. But EVIDENCE strengthening a DECISION has no representation at all. A capability whose check has passed on every run for six months says nothing about the Decision that chose that approach.
    OPTIONS: (a) symmetric credit assignment — the same GOVERNED_BY trace revise-trigger walks for bad news, walked for good news, so a decision accumulates a record of what has held up under it; (b) nothing stored, computed on read, the way `what_next` and the delivery line already are; (c) decline it — confidence scores invite exactly the ranking `dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable` refused, and a decision that looks strong because nothing has broken yet is survivorship bias with a number on it.
    ⚠️ (c) IS THE SERIOUS OBJECTION AND SHOULD NOT BE WAVED PAST. This design has already refused to store a score on alternatives once, deliberately. "Positive feedback strengthens a choice" is easy to say and easy to turn into a number that makes an untested road look worse than a lucky one.

📌 AND THE THIRD THING HE NAMED, ALREADY PARTLY ANSWERED ELSEWHERE: "testing reveals a facet the designer didn't initially consider". That is not doubt about a decision — it is a REQUIREMENT that was never written. `cap:missing-sibling` ("Notice the requirement nobody wrote down") is PLANNED and is the node for it.

properties.rationale: Recorded because a thorough search showed the return path is already designed in six nodes and unbuilt in two of them — so the useful contribution is not to re-describe it but to name the two places his ask genuinely exceeds it. The asymmetry in (2) is the more interesting of the two: this design has a rich vocabulary for things going wrong and almost none for things holding up, and it refused to score alternatives on purpose, so the obvious fix collides with a settled position.
